shot.Net.top: When your opponent drops short, meet it early and play a tight net shot back. It forces them to lift and hands you the attack.
shot.Net.bottom: You don't have to fight at the net every time. Push or lift past your opponent instead and make them move to the back.
shot.Lift.top: When you're under pressure, lift high to the back corners instead of forcing a drop. It buys you time to get back to the middle.
shot.Lift.bottom: Try not to lift the shuttle up and give your opponent an easy smash. Keep it low with a net shot or a push when you can.
shot.Smash.top: When you get a short, high lift, go for the smash. Aim at your opponent's body or the sidelines, not just hard down the middle.
shot.Smash.bottom: You don't have to smash every high shuttle. A clear or a well-placed drop keeps you in control without wearing you out.
shot.Drop.top: From the back, mix in drops so your opponent can't just wait deep. Make it look like a smash or a clear until the last moment.
shot.Drop.bottom: When you're at the back, don't feel you have to drop. A steep smash or a deep clear can do the same job with less risk.
shot.Clear.top: When you're stuck at the back, a high, deep clear resets the rally. Aim for the back line so your opponent can't attack it.
shot.Clear.bottom: Try not to clear when your opponent is waiting at the back. Use a drop or a smash to keep them moving instead.
shot.Drive.top: When the shuttle comes flat at shoulder height, drive it back flat and fast. It stops your opponent from getting set to attack.
shot.Drive.bottom: You don't have to swap flat drives. Lift high or block short to change the pace and break your opponent's rhythm.
shot.Push.top: When the shuttle is just above the net, push it flat into the midcourt gaps. It's hard to attack and keeps the pressure on.
shot.Push.bottom: Don't just push from the front. A tight net shot or a high lift gives your opponent something harder to deal with.
shot.Net kill.top: Stay close to the net with your racket up after a good net shot. If the reply floats up, hit it down straight away.
shot.Net kill.bottom: You don't have to rush every loose net reply. A controlled net shot or push is safer than a kill into the tape.
band.short.strength: Make the first few shots count. A tight serve and a sharp third shot can win the point before the rally settles.
band.short.weakness: Watch the serve and the return closely. Most short rallies are lost on the first couple of shots, so get your racket up early.
band.mid.strength: Once the rally has settled, look for the first loose shot and attack it. Don't wait for a perfect chance.
band.mid.weakness: Once the rally settles, don't rush the attack. Keep the shuttle deep or low until you get a really loose reply.
band.long.strength: Be patient in long rallies. Keep the shuttle deep and safe, get back to the middle after every shot, and wait for your opponent to make the mistake.
band.long.weakness: If long rallies wear you down, go for a safe, deep shot and recover to the middle. Try to end the point when you get an easy chance rather than waiting.
